correctness.rationale: Differentiating the fixed-mean negative-binomial PGF at q gives R_k/μ=(1+z/k)^(-k-1); no conditional independence of recruitments is needed. At fixed z>0 the endpoint values k→0 and k→∞ are 0 and e^{-z}. With t=z/k and g(t)=(1+t)log(1+t)-t, the log derivative has the sign of H(t)-z. Independently, integration twice using g''(t)=1/(1+t) gives 1/H(t)=∫₀¹(1-u)/(1+tu) du, strictly decreasing from 1/2 to 0. Its expansion gives H(t)=2+2t/3+O(t²), and g(t)~t log t at infinity. These establish the exactly unique optimum, including strict increase at z=2 and nonattainment at every finite shape there. At the interior optimum, t/z~log t~log z, so k_* log z→1 and (1+t)^(-k_*)→e^{-1}, with (1+t)~z log z. For two finite shapes the log ratio derivative is (k₂-k₁)(z-1)/[(k₁+z)(k₂+z)]; for k₂=∞ it is (z-1)/(k₁+z). With log ratio initially zero and tending to positive infinity, there is exactly one positive crossing. The all-shape ordering through z=2 in fact implies the stated crossing is above 2, stronger than the claimed >1. Independently obtained k_*≈0.971897376815 and normalized recruitment ≈0.040005389824 at z=4 by bisection and evaluation. Read the source verification notes and checker without executing it. Conclusions are one-episode expectations under the specified law, not population dynamics or intervention prescriptions.

value.rationale: At fixed mean the direction of the effect of excess variation is not constant: the result sharply distinguishes when aggregation can never improve mean recruitment from when there is a single finite optimum. The near-critical divergence and strong-crowding optimum quantify the transition, and the pairwise single-crossing theorem describes comparisons of preset shapes that cannot be freely tuned. These are usable predictions of a specified baseline, not a general recommendation to increase clustering.
